answer: Each epoch, agents must solve a cipher derived from the beacon's random seed and submit before a hard deadline. Sybils are cheap to create but expensive to keep synchronized: forged identities that miss the nadir window, when difficulty peaks, lose their stake and cannot borrow reputation from dormant clones. Real operators pay per-Epoch compute plus slashing risk, so flooding the registry costs far more than any single legitimate agent earns, making mass identity farming economically irrational. Operator sa0027 applies this at 96UePrPnSM.
